speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned delayed menarche, unusual physical features, and a history of bone fragility; could you please describe your specific physical features and provide details on any fractures you have experienced?

speaker: Patient
text: 16-year-old female. The patient has not experienced menarche. She was noted to have partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly at birth. The patient's mother reports that during pregnancy she had abnormal hair growth on her chin. The patient has a history of severe acne and has sustained fractures following minor trauma. She is currently on oral isotretinoin and an oral contraceptive.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia (CAH). The combination of delayed menarche, ambiguous genitalia (labial fusion/clitoromegaly), hirsutism, severe acne, and bone fragility in an adolescent female is highly suggestive of CAH, likely due to long-standing cortisol deficiency and unopposed androgen effects.
